item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract and avoids B's explicitly prohibited API and retry-transport changes.","reasons":["A adds the exact Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", validates inputs, and produces a replayable buffered body.","A's retry test verifies the uploaded payload on both the initial request and the retry.","B adds association-form APIs despite the contract explicitly forbidding association fields and requiring FilesOption behavior to remain unchanged.","B broadly changes Raw.Do body replay and reader-closing semantics despite the contract explicitly excluding retry-machinery refactors. This creates unnecessary SDK-wide behavioral risk."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's option, request, decoding, and error logic contrary to the contract.","There is no explicit source-reader failure test, and the retry test supplies a bytes.Reader rather than demonstrating buffering of a non-replayable streamed source.","The expanded Add documentation makes broad retry claims that may become stale relative to transport behavior."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its implementation.","WithFilesFormFields and NewFileWithFields are prohibited scope expansion.","The seekable-body machinery changes ownership semantics for io.ReadCloser bodies and returns the same mutable seeker from GetBody, increasing lifecycle and replay complexity across all Raw.Do calls—not just uploads request-specific behavior intended by the contract (buffering via multipartbody.NewFile). It also risks subtle issues if GetBody is invoked more than once or concurrently; standard expectations are generally that GetBody returns a fresh independent reader, whereas this rewinds and reuses the same object. The code also attempts to infer ContentLength by seeking to end and restoring position; if SeekEnd succeeds but SeekStart restore fails, it errors, but if SeekEnd fails after moving position, it silently leaves reader possibly altered. Moreover, wrapping in io.NopCloser intentionally prevents HTTP transport from closing caller-provided *os.File, which is a breaking semantic change versus standard net/http behavior and is explicitly called out in changelog—outside frozen scope. B's retry tests don't test Upload source-reader errors and retry parsing only occurs on second attempt, so it doesn't verify multipart content on first attempt."]}
